talk.title: Algorithms and Computation
talk.notes:
Algorithms and Computation (lecture)
[1:13] Cue: What are the course goals?
[3:36] Cue: What is a computational problem?
[3:36] A problem is a binary relation from inputs to correct outputs.
[9:40] An algorithm is a procedure mapping each input to a single output; it is correct if that output is correct for every input.
[15:20] Correctness of a recursive algorithm is shown by induction.
[24:10] Efficiency is measured asymptotically, counting constant-time operations in the Word-RAM model.
Summary: problems, algorithms, correctness by induction, asymptotic efficiency.
